description: An exemplar of what is ecologically possible in a Boroondara residential garden. Sam's Canterbury property has been cultivated over a decade into a genuine biodiversity corridor node — 30 indigenous species spanning all five structural layers, a closed-loop water system, embedded habitat complexity, and confirmed fauna including Superb Fairywren, Eastern Spinebill and Common Brushtail Possum. The garden carries the highest ecological function score in the Ecological Registry and is recognised as a confirmed corridor node within the Boroondara cluster.

soil_water.mulch_type: Arborist mulch — self-generating from garden prunings

habitat.planting_method: Deep ecological planting across five structural layers — canopy trees, understorey shrubs, mid-layer grasses and forbs, groundcovers, and climbers — with all layers now self-seeding and self-sustaining. Established over a decade with consistent ecological management.

fauna_sightings.notes: Breeding pair confirmed nesting in Leptospermum hedge. Documented by G&S site visit.
Regular foraging visitor to Correa and Indigofera. Confirmed during G&S assessment.
Active nesting in installed nest box. Documented by G&S site visit.

activity_log.title: G&S ecological assessment — corridor node confirmed
activity_log.notes: Full site assessment by Gardener & Son. Garden assessed across all five scoring pillars. 30 indigenous species confirmed across five structural layers. Superb Fairywren nesting pair and possum nest box occupancy documented. Rainwater collection, seasonal moisture basin, and swale all functioning. Garden confirmed as a corridor node in the Boroondara ecological network. Score: 97/100.

activity_log.title: Breeding Superb Fairywren confirmed
activity_log.notes: Breeding pair of Superb Fairywren documented nesting in established Leptospermum continentale hedge. First confirmed nesting record for this garden. Possum nest box occupancy also confirmed on the same visit.

activity_log.title: Water feature and swale installed
activity_log.notes: Seasonal moisture basin and garden swale installed to close the water cycle. Combined with existing 5,000L rainwater tank, the garden now manages all rainfall on-site.

activity_log.title: 30th indigenous species established
activity_log.notes: Pratia puberula (Hairy Pratia) planted as the 30th locally indigenous species, completing the groundcover layer. All five structural layers now occupied by indigenous species. Indigenous species dominant across the planting.

notes: Highest-scoring garden in the Ecological Registry. Field notes (full written inventory) are the only outstanding evidence gap — all other evidence criteria met. Area to be formally surveyed; 650m2 is an estimate.

yield.formula_note: Score x area x connectivity x verification. Formula v1. Corridor node premium applied.
